name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,539

clue.text: Criminal chasing fellow gangster gets bird

indicators.note: something chasing comes behind what it pursues, so this piece goes last

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A crook pursuing another gangster ends up in jail, doing bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' tells you the criminal comes after the other two pieces. 'Bird' looks like slang for prison time but is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon is a bird of prey, so this is an example of the general class.

clue.text: Blend of fuel key to energy

blocks.note: coal is a fuel
the Escape key on a keyboard
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Mixing fuels may be the key to future energy supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blend' reads as a noun, but it is the verb, and 'to' simply strings the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to merge or come together into one mass, a verb synonym for mixing together.

clue.text: Privileged American class used to be soft

blocks.note: past tense of to be
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A comment that America's elite has gone soft.
explanation.definitionFit: WASP stands for White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, the traditional US social elite.

clue.text: Noise of passing wind - so who's being funny?

indicators.note: something behaving funny is acting strangely, out of its normal order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A rude noise prompts the question of which joker is responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing wind' invites a schoolboy reading; it is just air rushing by.
explanation.definitionFit: A swoosh is the rushing sound of something moving swiftly through air.

clue.text: Bond supports sombre dress code

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: black is a sombre colour
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond is the model for formal, sombre evening wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, who famously wears this outfit, but here it just means a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tie is the formal evening dress code printed on invitations, requiring dinner jackets.

clue.text: Repeat courses concerning green students

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
freshers are new first-year students at a British university

explanation.surface: Some inexperienced students are having to retake their classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Refresher courses go over material again to bring knowledge up to date.

clue.text: Amazon victory gets paramilitaries shot

blocks.note: V for victory
the Irish Republican Army
a go or shot is an attempt

explanation.surface: A news item about a winner's victory leading to gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' looks like the company or river; here it is a fierce warrior woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a strong, aggressive, domineering woman, after the mythical female warriors.

clue.text: Saved then cashed in

blocks.note: first meaning: rescued, delivered from sin
second meaning: exchanged a voucher or bond for money

explanation.surface: Someone put money aside, then withdrew it.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both spiritual rescue and exchanging coupons or bonds for their cash value.

clue.text: Bouquet offered by a gypsy

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roma are the Romani people

explanation.surface: A traveller hawking flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but it means a wine's smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic scent, so it is a synonym for a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Weaselly type of animal lover turning heads in Bordeaux perhaps

indicators.note: the leading letters of the word are turned round, swapping their order
one piece placed in another is put inside it

blocks.note: Bordeaux is an example of a wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal lover is turning heads in the French wine region.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters of the lover swap places before going inside the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolverine is the largest member of the weasel family, the mustelids.

clue.text: Company plays lively WI music

indicators.note: lively letters jump about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band performs upbeat Caribbean songs.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the West Indies; the shuffled word sits between the two letters of the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of Afro-Caribbean song from Trinidad, music of the West Indies.

clue.text: Worry about horse butchery

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: care is anxiety or worry
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Concern over a horse being slaughtered.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnage is slaughter on a large scale, a synonym for wholesale butchery.

clue.text: Perhaps he is nuts storing nitrogen in military structure?

indicators.note: storing means holding something inside
perhaps signals that these letters could be arranged some other way

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Suspicion that a man hoarding chemicals in an army building is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated corrugated-iron shelter used by the army in wartime.

clue.text: Lure modern musicians to wear camp gear head to toe

indicators.note: the head letter moves to the toe, the very end of the word
whatever is worn goes around the wearer

blocks.note: a tent is camping gear
rap is a modern music style

explanation.surface: Persuading trendy musicians into camp clothing from head to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head to toe' looks like dress description but moves the first letter of the camp gear to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrapment is luring someone into committing an offence, a noun for enticement into a trap.

clue.text: Pastor might curb rage

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain or hold in, so the words hold the answer inside

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A clergyman may be able to control anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rage, shout and behave furiously, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Some art nouveau expert?

indicators.note: nouveau is French for new, so the letters take on a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a specialist in Art Nouveau design is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art nouveau' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the art joins 'Some', and nouveau is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially music, so an accomplished expert.

clue.text: Young lady transmitted quite unusual 'je ne sais quoi'

indicators.note: transmitted as in broadcast, so heard rather than read
unusual means not in the usual order

blocks.note: Miss is a title for a young lady
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl's broadcast had a rather special indefinable quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystique and the French phrase both describe an elusive, attractive quality that cannot be put into words.

clue.text: Variation of an older English flowering plant

indicators.note: a variation is a changed form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Talk of an older English variety of a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen Mediterranean shrub with showy pink or white blooms.

clue.text: On-line repair regularly needs to be adjusted

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

blocks.note: E as in e-mail stands for electronic, online
to mend is to repair
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An internet repair job routinely needs fine-tuning.
explanation.definitionFit: Emended means corrected or altered, usually of a text, so it is a synonym for amended.

clue.text: Brave society accepts Liberal luvvies

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: daring means bold, brave
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A bold club welcomes a Liberal politician among the theatre types.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the brave word takes in the Liberal; society is tacked on after.
explanation.definitionFit: Luvvie and darling are both terms of endearment, luvvie being British slang for an effusive actor.

clue.text: Capital Italy invested in place to relax

indicators.note: to invest in is to put into, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: a sofa is somewhere to sit and relax
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Italy has put money into a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'invested' suggest money, but capital is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Bulgarian seat of government is one of many national capital cities.

clue.text: Lots of dresses changing hands

indicators.note: the two hands are right and left, and one swaps for the other

blocks.note: frocks are dresses

explanation.surface: Lots of clothes being sold second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Flocks of things are large numbers or crowds, so it means lots as a plural noun.

clue.text: Listen into tip-off for what happens in Autumn

indicators.note: the tip, the front end, is taken off

blocks.note: in autumn the leaves drop from trees

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops to get a tip-off about an autumn event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip-off' reads as a piece of inside information, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen in secretly on a private conversation.

clue.text: Conceit of old Queen and her Prince sounds lousy

indicators.note: sounds tells you the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: Victoria and Albert, as in the V&A museum
nitty means infested with nits, lice

explanation.surface: Remark that Victoria and Albert's vanity seems contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is an excessive pride in oneself, an exact synonym for vanity.

clue.text: Charlie's jazzy pen name?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pseudonym a musician called Charlie might write under
setter's reading: the surname of the jazz saxophonist Charlie 'Bird', which is also a famous brand of fountain pen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen name' suggests a pseudonym; read it instead as the name on a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The bebop saxophonist shares his surname with a well-known pen manufacturer.

clue.text: Hear of mettle shown by male endurance winner

indicators.note: hear tells you to take the word by its sound

blocks.note: mettle sounds like metal, and iron is an example of a metal
a man is a male

explanation.surface: Talk of a man showing his mettle by winning a gruelling contest.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironman triathlon is a gruelling long-distance race, and its champion bears the title.

clue.text: Nylon top provided layer that's more stylish

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter
if means provided that
a tier is a layer

explanation.surface: A nylon top worn over another layer looks smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a garment, but it takes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty means neat, smart and stylish, so the comparative is more stylish.

clue.text: Little fish ingesting uranium causes anger

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, taking something inside

blocks.note: fry are young fish
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Pollution from a nuclear plant entering fish stocks provokes outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is violent rage, so it is a stronger synonym for anger.

clue.text: Extremely cruel bounders leaving punk in destitution

indicators.note: the outer bounding letters are left behind, keeping what lies within

blocks.note: the run of letters inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Cads abandoning a penniless punk is a heartless act.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounders look like cads but are the boundaries of the phrase. Shakespeare's 'the most unkindest cut of all' is the echo.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkindest is the superlative of unkind, so it means cruel to the greatest degree.

clue.text: Reprobate German leader seduced by French libertine

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
something seduced is taken in by another, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a roué is a debauched man, a French word
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A German politician led astray by a French rake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled person, the same sense as a reprobate.
